I am building a KTOR based Web Application in a Monorepo using the following structure.

app/
  ktor-api/
    Ktor RestAPI and backend to be hosted on Google Cloud under the subdomain `api.sedaia-designs.org`. The domain `sedaia-designs` is held by vercel, and owned by me.
solidjs-v2-business/
	A SolidJS V2 Web Application deployed using Vercel's services, uses the domain `sedaia-designs.org`
solidjs-v2-portfolio/
	A SolidJS V2 Static Webpage that makes calls to the Ktor API
sql-db/
	**Yet to be made**: A Sql based database that contains static information on Images, Text Content, and resource locations
cdn/
	**Yet to be made**: A Content Delivery Solution that will host all the images. As this part hasn't been made yet, all images will be embedded in the SolidJS applications.

The goal is to publish only the `ktor-api` to google cloud for now, as Vercel can only deploy NodeJS based web applications. The SQL-DB will also very likely be hosted on gcloud, so I would like to setup the necessary stubs I can later hook onto when making that setup.

The Code is hosted on GitLab, where it can be accessed by both Vercel and GCloud

The solution focuses on deploying the KTOR API to Google Cloud and setting up the foundation for a SQL database and CDN. Cloud Run is an excellent choice for the KTOR API due to its fully managed nature, autoscaling capabilities, and support for containerized applications, aligning with the need to deploy the `ktor-api` as a container. Cloud Build will automate the process of creating and updating the container image for the KTOR API. For the future SQL database, Cloud SQL provides a fully managed relational database service that can be easily integrated. For the CDN, Cloud Storage can serve as a robust and scalable solution for hosting static images and content. Cloud Logging and Cloud Monitoring will be essential for observing the health and performance of the deployed services. The Cloud SDK will be used for command-line interactions and automation.

Here's a list of step-by-step guide to solve the problem:

- **Prepare KTOR API for Containerization**: Ensure your `ktor-api` project is set up to be containerized, typically by creating a Dockerfile.
- **Automate Container Image Creation with [Cloud Build](https://cloud.google.com/#)**: Configure Cloud Build to automatically build a Docker image for your `ktor-api` whenever changes are pushed to your repository. This image will be stored in a container registry.
- **Deploy KTOR API to [Cloud Run](https://cloud.google.com/#)**: Use Cloud Run to deploy the containerized `ktor-api`. Configure Cloud Run to use the image built by Cloud Build.
- **Configure Custom Domain for Cloud Run**: Map the `api.sedaia-designs.org` subdomain to your deployed Cloud Run service. This will involve verifying domain ownership and updating DNS records.
- **Set up [Cloud SQL](https://cloud.google.com/#) Instance (Stub)**: Create a Cloud SQL instance (e.g., PostgreSQL or MySQL) to serve as the future database for your application. While not immediately used, this establishes the necessary infrastructure.
- **Set up [Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/#) Bucket for CDN (Stub)**: Create a Cloud Storage bucket to host static assets like images. Configure it for public access if needed for your CDN strategy.
- **Implement Logging and Monitoring**: Enable [Cloud Logging](https://cloud.google.com/#) and [Cloud Monitoring](https://cloud.google.com/#) for your Cloud Run service and Cloud SQL instance to track application performance, errors, and resource utilization.
- **Utilize [Cloud SDK](https://cloud.google.com/#) for Management**: Use the Cloud SDK for command-line interactions, scripting deployments, and managing your Google Cloud resources.
